ranking_note: Authored from the before descriptions at commit 3e2d300ad331d7dfd63f399486154edd370a07aa, frozen before any rewrite; protocol per /playbooks:skill-authoring ## Measurement. Competitors are prototype:pressure-test (a throwaway terminal app or HTML demo stepping business logic, state or a data model through awkward cases), user-interface:design (designing CLI output, TUIs, banners and app UI from the project's design system), visualization:visualize (choosing and rendering a diagram, chart or table for conversation content), playgrounds:use (the first-party interactive parameter explorer whose output is a prompt to paste back), user-experience:structure (user flows, information architecture, navigation and sitemaps), user-experience:evaluate (usability evaluation of an existing design, flow or app), user-interface:write-css (writing and reviewing CSS against the project's tokens), prototype:build-generator (a tunable throwaway generator for an artifact prompting cannot hit) and planning:brainstorm (diverging into candidate engineering or product approaches before scope is locked). explore-directions owns building a few structurally different throwaway layouts of one screen, switchable in place, to decide what it should look like.

queries.request: We can't agree whether the orders page should be a dense table or a grid of cards. Can you build a few versions I can flip between?
Before I commit to anything for the onboarding dashboard, I'd like to see three quite different takes on how it could be arranged.
Where would a returns panel fit on our account page? Throw together a couple of alternatives I can click through.
I have no idea how the analytics overview screen should be organized. Give me some rough arrangements to try before we pick one.
Prototype a handful of directions for the new invoice detail page in a standalone HTML file I can open without running anything.
Our team keeps arguing from whiteboard sketches about the settings screen. Can you make clickable alternatives so we can choose?
Build a few competing versions of the checkout summary behind ?variant= on the real cart route so we can judge them with live data.
What could the empty, loading and error states of the inbox page look like? Show me several divergent approaches I can toggle.
I want to see some alternative arrangements for the team members page before we settle on one and build it properly.
Sketch three competing structures for a parcel tracking screen with a toggle so the product owner can try each one.
Spin up a little terminal app so I can step through whether a subscription can be paused while a payment retry is still pending.
How should our CLI's error output look when a config file fails to parse, and when should it use color?
Draw a diagram of the request flow we just talked through between the gateway, the auth service and billing.
Make me an interactive explorer with sliders for tuning an easing curve, and hand me back a prompt with the values I settle on.
Draft a sitemap for the admin area: which sections live under settings, billing and team, and how the navigation nests.
Write the CSS for the pricing card component using our existing spacing and color tokens.
The noise texture behind our hero keeps coming out wrong however I describe it. Give me something with knobs I can tune, then save the result into the repo.
Give me some rough ideas for how we could cut support tickets about password resets, cheapest first.
Run a heuristic evaluation of our live checkout and list the usability problems by severity.
Style the warning banner our PowerShell module prints so it reads well in both dark and light terminals.
